subject: Production: OrbitPay EU checkout — proxy queue saturation and 502/503s

Cc: ops@orbitpay.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production edge failures impacting EU checkout - urgent

Hi Ava / Redwood ops,

We're seeing a sustained spike of 502 / 503 / 504 responses from your EU edge since ~06:30 UTC this morning. Error rate is ~12% for requests to /v1/generate for our checkout flow (region eu-west). Customers are experiencing timeouts and some duplicate charges because our retry logic kicks in when we see 502/503 + 429.

Examples (request ids): OP-req-6a1f2, OP-req-6a1f9, OP-req-6a24b — all show 502 returned from redwood-eu-edge-01 and 503 from redwood-eu-proxy-05. We're attaching our capture and some logs.

Impact: our conversion dropped sharply for two hours, operations is getting paged. This is a high-severity incident for us; can you confirm receipt and provide immediate mitigations (route to fallback region, reduce retries, or any hotfix) and an ETA on full restore?

I'm available on +44 7700 900111 — please call if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitPay

Subject: Re: Production edge failures impacting EU checkout - diagnostic notes

A quick diagnostic summary from the runtime team (current snapshot):

Observations:
- Proxy queue depth on redwood-eu-proxy-05 and -06 rose to >95th percentile at 06:22 UTC, sustained through 08:10 UTC.
- We saw a burst of small, chat-like requests (median seq length 48 tokens) generated in a narrow timespan from a handful of client IP blocks associated with OrbitPay's rollout.
- Per-proxy upstream connection pools hit their per-node connection limit; new upstream attempts were failing and returning 502/503.
- KV cache miss rate increased (cache warming thrash), which caused higher backend compute demand and longer service times, compounding the queueing.
- Retry storms from client-side exponential-backoff misconfiguration amplified the transient failures into multi-minute outage windows.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30 UTC):
- Increased proxy_conn_limit on affected proxies; added temporary headroom for 72 hours.
- Enabled soft-fallback routing for OrbitPay traffic to eu-central model pool (partial shift, ~25% of sessions) to reduce load on saturated nodes.
- Applied transient rate-limiter rule for repeated identical request hashes from the same IP to curb retry loops.

Recommended next steps:
- OrbitPay to throttle client retries for 60 minutes during recovery window.
- We should provision a short Dedicated burst (1x A100-equivalent pool) for OrbitPay for the next 72 hours while we reconfigure caches and observe normal traffic shape.
- Postmortem to confirm root cause (interaction of small-seq workload + cache misses + connection pool exhaustion).

Attached: trimmed edge logs (edge-debug-logs-20270107.txt). I'll push a more detailed analysis to SUP-4321.

— Grace O'Connor
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
